clue.text: Astute little creature died

blocks.note: a shrew is a tiny mouse-like mammal
D is the standard abbreviation for died, as in family trees

explanation.surface: A clever small animal has passed away.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone shrewd has sharp practical judgement, which is what being astute means.

clue.text: Draw a match, draw about five

indicators.note: about means going round, so one word wraps itself around the other piece

blocks.note: to hale is an old verb meaning to drag or haul, a sense of draw
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A sports report: a match ends level, the score something like five each.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated 'draw' changes sense: first a tied result, then pulling, as in to hale someone into court.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf, to halve a match is to finish level with the opponent, the equivalent of a tied game.

clue.text: The old vessel hidden by the rising plant

indicators.note: something hidden by another thing sits inside it, so these pieces go within the next
in a down clue, rising means read from bottom to top, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: ye is the archaic spelling of the
a brig is a two-masted sailing ship
taken as written, then turned upward

explanation.surface: An antique ship lies concealed behind a growing plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyebright is a small meadow herb, once used to treat sore eyes, hence its name.

clue.text: Club must have a licence

definitions.note: a description of the answer rather than a synonym

blocks.note: first meaning: the golf club used for long tee shots
second meaning: a person at the wheel of a car, who legally needs a permit

explanation.surface: A rule that a golf club or society can only operate with a licence.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the longest-hitting golf wood and anyone who operates a motor vehicle, who needs a permit.

clue.text: Joe Miller's horse?

definitions.note: the possessive stands for the sort of thing found in Joe Miller's joke book

blocks.note: first meaning: a stale, much-repeated joke; Joe Miller's Jests was a famous eighteenth-century joke book
second meaning: a reddish-brown horse

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a question about who owns a horse; Joe Miller was an actor whose name was put on a jest book, and a Joe Miller became a byword for an old joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A chestnut is an overfamiliar joke, exactly the stock of Joe Miller's book, and also a horse of reddish-brown colouring.

clue.text: Flowers heard in Kent at times

definitions.note: a description: the chimes of the cathedral city, not a synonym

blocks.note: first meaning: a garden plant with bell-shaped blue or white blooms
second meaning, taken literally: the ringing of the cathedral bells in that Kentish city

explanation.walkthrough: Canterbury is the cathedral city in Kent, the county in south-east England, so its bells are literally heard there at times.
explanation.definitionFit: Canterbury bells are a campanula, a garden plant with tall spikes of bell-like blooms, named after the city.

clue.text: River cries out for use

indicators.note: out suggests something put out of order, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, a crossword favourite
the five letters of this word, rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone by a river calls out for help or for something to be used.
explanation.definitionFit: To exercise a right or power is to use it, as in exercising one's judgement.

clue.text: Sum me up - I'm revered in North America

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom, so it runs backwards

blocks.note: to tot up is to add up a sum
taken as written, then turned upward

explanation.surface: Someone asking to be summed up in a few words, as though a revered North American figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' does double duty: tot up is to add, and in a down light it also lifts ME into EM.
explanation.definitionFit: A totem is a natural object or animal venerated as an emblem by a clan among Indigenous peoples of North America.

clue.text: Valuers in disarray, without exception

indicators.note: things in disarray are jumbled and disordered, so these letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written: it also forms part of the indicator phrase in the surface

explanation.surface: Every one of the valuers is in a muddle.
explanation.walkthrough: The word 'in' is used twice: as letters in the mix and as part of 'in disarray'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something universal applies to all cases with none left out, hence without exception.

clue.text: State in which I can switch adherence

indicators.note: in which says the next letters go inside the word just given
to switch things around is to change their order, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: to allege is to state or assert
these three letters plus I, rearranged

explanation.surface: A nation where a person may change loyalty freely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a country, matching the surface theme of loyalty, but it is the verb meaning assert.
explanation.definitionFit: Allegiance is loyalty or faithful support owed to a cause or ruler, which is what adherence means.

clue.text: Dog, or part of a dog

blocks.note: first meaning: as a verb, to follow someone closely
second meaning: the wagging end of the animal

explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Dog' is a verb, to shadow someone, not the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: To tail a suspect is to follow them closely, as detectives do, and a tail is also the hindmost appendage of a hound.

clue.text: One always around for each recurrent rescue

indicators.note: around means one word wraps the single letter given before it
recurrent is taken as running back, so the whole string is read in reverse

blocks.note: ever means always, as in ever hopeful
I is the Roman numeral for one
per means for each, as in miles per gallon

explanation.surface: Someone who keeps coming back to save each person in turn.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprieve is a last-minute rescue from punishment, especially a cancelled or postponed execution.

clue.text: Wave provided by hair-dresser (6

blocks.note: first meaning: a long curling sea wave that breaks on the shore
second meaning: read literally, one who dresses hair with a comb

explanation.surface: A hair wave created at the salon.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen splits hairdresser into a person who dresses hair, that is, one who combs it.
explanation.definitionFit: A comber is a long rolling breaker at sea, and literally anyone or anything that combs.

clue.text: Catch on a little bit of wood

blocks.note: first meaning: informally, to understand or realise
second meaning: a slender shoot from a branch

explanation.surface: Something snags on a small piece of timber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catch on' looks like snagging, but it is the phrasal verb for understanding; twig in this sense is British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: To twig is colloquial British for grasping a point suddenly, and a twig is also a small thin stick from a tree.

clue.text: Shapely spring found

blocks.note: a spring is a natural source of water, as is a well
to found a business is to set it up

explanation.surface: A curvaceous spring has been discovered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found' looks like the past of find; here it is the verb meaning establish.
explanation.definitionFit: Well set-up describes someone with a strong, well-built figure, which fits shapely.

clue.text: Man is killed, primarily, by its eyes

definitions.text: Man is killed, primarily, by its eyes

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter of the word before is used

blocks.note: Basil is a man's name
taken as written
the opening letter of this word

explanation.surface: A warning that the creature's gaze is fatal to humans.
explanation.walkthrough: Taken whole, the clue describes the creature: a man is chiefly killed by its eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: The basilisk is a mythical serpent whose mere look was said to kill anyone who met its gaze.

clue.text: It illuminates Elia's verbal promise

indicators.note: verbal means spoken in words, so the phrase is judged by how it is said

blocks.note: Elia was the pen name of the essayist Charles Lamb
a plight is a pledge, as in plighting one's troth

explanation.surface: Something casts light on a promise made by the writer Elia.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, Lamb's plight runs together as lamplight.
explanation.definitionFit: Lamplight is the glow given off by a lamp, so it is something that lights up a room.

clue.text: Used in the wardrobe - sandalwood?

blocks.note: surface reading: a fragrant timber, perhaps used to scent a wardrobe
setter's reading: wood for sandals, a wooden form placed inside footwear to keep its shape

explanation.walkthrough: Sandalwood suggests a scented timber for a cupboard; split it as wood for sandals.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoe tree is a shaped wooden insert that keeps footwear in form while stored in a cupboard.

clue.text: He produced missiles, aided by Beaumont

definitions.note: a description of the playwright rather than a synonym

blocks.note: first meaning: a maker of arrows
second meaning: the Jacobean dramatist John who co-wrote plays with Francis Beaumont

explanation.walkthrough: Beaumont and Fletcher were a famous playwriting partnership of the early seventeenth century.
explanation.definitionFit: A fletcher is an arrow-maker, the arrows being the missiles, and John Fletcher was Beaumont's writing partner.

clue.text: Scottish island promontory

blocks.note: first meaning: an island of the Inner Hebrides
second meaning: a Scottish word for a headland

explanation.definitionFit: Mull is a large Hebridean isle, and in Scottish place names a mull is a headland jutting into the sea.

clue.text: Midget is quiet, right? I'm quiet

blocks.note: sh is the call for silence
R is the abbreviation for right
taken as written, without the apostrophe
p, for piano, is the musical marking for soft

explanation.surface: A small person checks they are being quiet enough.
explanation.walkthrough: The two 'quiet's give different letters: one the hush, the other the musical direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrimp is an informal, slightly mocking word for a very small person.

clue.text: Hope to be a part of church

blocks.note: taken as written
a spire is the tapering top of a church tower

explanation.surface: Someone wishing to become a member of a church.
explanation.definitionFit: To aspire is to set one's heart on achieving something, a verb close to hope or long.

clue.text: Maybe cast gold in, and won)

blocks.note: taken as written
got means obtained or won

explanation.surface: Perhaps gold was thrown in and the game won.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' looks like throw, but here it means poured into a mould.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingot is a block of metal formed in a mould, gold being one example, hence the maybe.

clue.text: Having ruined blonde he is under an" obligation

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked out of shape, so these letters are put in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man who has wronged a blonde woman now owes her.
explanation.definitionFit: Beholden means indebted, owing a favour or duty to someone.

clue.text: To be beheaded, male chauvinist pig

indicators.note: beheaded means the head is cut off, so the opening letter is dropped

blocks.note: a male chauvinist pig is a man with sexist attitudes

explanation.surface: A cry that a chauvinist man deserves to lose his head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To be' looks like a fragment of a sentence, but it is the infinitive verb the answer replaces.
explanation.definitionFit: To exist is to have being or reality, the plain sense of the verb to be.

clue.text: Without females the theatre is incomplete

indicators.note: incomplete means not whole, so the final letter of the word is dropped

blocks.note: the stage stands for the theatre as a profession

explanation.surface: A theatre company lacking actresses is short-handed.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag party or event is one attended by men only, a gathering with no women present.

clue.text: No plain girl worked without a -kitchen tool

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the following letter is taken out of the mix
worked means kneaded or reshaped, so these letters are formed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written, the letter removed

explanation.surface: An attractive girl got on with the job without a pastry utensil.
explanation.definitionFit: A rolling pin is a cylinder used in cooking to flatten dough, a standard kitchen utensil.

clue.text: Lady Macbeth was not so pure

definitions.note: a cryptic description: she was never free of the mark on her hand

blocks.note: first meaning, cryptic: she could not rid her hand of the blood, crying 'Out, damned spot!'
second meaning: clean, unblemished, without stain

explanation.walkthrough: In the sleepwalking scene Lady Macbeth tries in vain to wash a bloodstain from her hand, so she was never free of marks.
explanation.definitionFit: Spotless means perfectly clean and, figuratively, morally unblemished or pure.

clue.text: One wearing a jacket underground

blocks.note: surface reading: a person in a coat on the subway, or a secret agent
setter's reading: a vegetable baked in its skin, which grows in soil

explanation.walkthrough: A jacket is the skin of a baked tuber; 'underground' is where it grows, not a railway or resistance movement.
explanation.definitionFit: A potato grows as a tuber beneath the soil and is often served baked in its skin, called a jacket.
